title: Blood Relations

steps.title: Understanding family trees
steps.content: Blood relation problems ask you to determine the relationship between two people based on given information. Draw a family tree diagram to visualize relationships. Use only the facts stated—never assume gender or side of the family without evidence.
steps.example: If A is B's father and B is C's mother, then A is C's maternal grandfather.
steps.tip: Start from the reference person in the sentence and add one link at a time.

steps.title: Identify the relationship
steps.prompt: A man points to a girl and says: “She is the daughter of my father's only son.” How is the girl related to the man?
steps.explanation: The man's father's only son is the man himself. The girl is his daughter.
hints: Start from the person named after 'my'.

steps.title: Follow a short chain
steps.prompt: A is B's brother. C is A's father. D is C's father. How is D related to B?
steps.explanation: C is B's father. D is C's father, so D is B's grandfather.
hints: Draw the tree from the youngest generation upward.

steps.title: Common relationship chains
steps.content: Father's father → Grandfather. Father's mother → Grandmother. Mother's father → Maternal grandfather. Father's brother → Uncle. Father's sister → Aunt. Track maternal vs paternal when the sentence provides the side.
steps.tip: For complex chains, break them: Person X → relation Y → relation Z → target.

steps.title: Complex chain
steps.prompt: A's mother is the sister of B. B's father is the son of C. Assuming the siblings share both parents, how is C related to A?
steps.explanation: B's father is also A's mother's father. That man is C's son, so C is one generation above A's maternal grandfather: A's great-grandparent.
hints: Trace from the final named person back to the asked person.

steps.title: Solve a statement safely
steps.content: A methodical order prevents generation jumps.
steps.prompt: Arrange the steps for a typical blood-relation statement.
options: Add each stated link to a tree
steps.explanation: Read, anchor the reference person, draw links, then answer.
hints: Never answer before the tree is complete.
The reference person is usually introduced by my/his/her.

steps.title: Gender-neutral answer
steps.prompt: A is the father of B. B is the sister of C. C is the brother of D. How is D related to A?
steps.explanation: B, C and D are children of A. D's gender is not specified, so D is A's child.
hints: Do not invent a gender for D.
Choose the most precise answer supported by the facts.

steps.title: Catch an assumption error
steps.content: A student assumes every sibling of a parent is an uncle.
steps.code:
parent_sibling_gender = 'sister'
label = 'uncle' if parent_sibling_gender == 'brother' else 'aunt'
print(label)
options: A parent's sister is an aunt; gender must be used when given
Siblings of parents are never related

feedback_by_option.1: Correct. Use gender clues: brother → uncle, sister → aunt.
feedback_by_option.2: They are related; the issue is the exact label.
feedback_by_option.3: Cousins are a different generation relationship.
feedback_by_option.4: Aunts are valid and common in these questions.

hints: Ask whether the sentence states brother or sister.
Do not default every parental sibling to uncle.

steps.title: Maternal vs paternal
steps.prompt: Ravi is Sita's brother. Sita is Mohan's mother. How is Ravi related to Mohan?
steps.explanation: Sita is Mohan's mother. Her brother Ravi is Mohan's maternal uncle.
hints: The parent's brother on the mother's side is the maternal uncle.

questions.prompt: A man says: “The lady is the daughter of my father's only son.” How is the lady related to the man?
questions.explanation: Father's only son is the man himself; the lady is his daughter.

questions.prompt: A is the father of B. B is the sister of C. C is the brother of D. How is D related to A?
questions.explanation: D's gender is not specified; D is A's child.

questions.prompt: Anu is Bala's mother. Bala is Charan's father. How is Anu related to Charan?
Ravi is Sita's brother. Sita is Mohan's mother. How is Ravi related to Mohan?
P is Q's daughter. Q is R's son. What is P's relation to R?
A is B's brother. C is A's father. D is C's father. How is D related to B?

srs_cards.question: How do you solve blood relation problems systematically?
srs_cards.answer: Draw a family tree. Start from the reference person. Add one relationship at a time. Use only stated gender facts.

srs_cards.question: Why must you not assume every parental sibling is an uncle?
srs_cards.answer: A parent's sister is an aunt; gender must be respected when given.

srs_cards.question: What should you do when gender is not stated?
srs_cards.answer: Prefer a gender-neutral label such as child when that is the most precise supported answer.

learning_objectives: Translate family statements into a family-tree diagram.
Track maternal and paternal relationships across generations.
Use gender information without assuming unstated facts.
Solve multi-step family relationship questions accurately.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A sibling of a parent is always an uncle regardless of gender.
common_misconceptions.correction: A parent's brother is an uncle and a parent's sister is an aunt.

common_misconceptions.misconception: The speaker's gender can be assumed from the sentence.
A relationship chain should be read only left to right.
common_misconceptions.correction: Anchor the reference person first and trace each pronoun carefully.

worked_examples.title: Follow two relationships
worked_examples.input: A is B's mother. B is C's brother.
trace: A is one generation above B.
worked_examples.explanation: Represent each relation as an edge in a small family tree.

worked_examples.title: Track paternal relation
worked_examples.input: P is the father of Q. Q is the sister of R.
trace: P is also father of R.
worked_examples.explanation: Sibling relationships connect the same parent group when established.

worked_examples.title: Avoid unsupported assumptions
trace: Side and gender are not stated.
worked_examples.output: Do not infer more than cousin
worked_examples.explanation: A correct answer uses only the facts provided.

company_applications.practice: Sketch each generation and mark genders explicitly.
Translate pronouns into a diagram before selecting an option.
Avoid assuming relationships that are not stated.
Prefer gender-neutral answers when gender is unknown.

quest.story: Service-company reasoning rounds hide generation traps inside short statements. Turn each sentence into a tree so the relationship is proven rather than guessed.
quest.mission: Track generations, gender clues and family links using a small diagram.
success_criteria: Identify the reference person in a statement.
Draw parent, child and sibling links.
Resolve multi-step relationship chains without illegal assumptions.
